ClientResponses.Response: Thank you for your feedback and for taking the time to review our Timberline 1300. We understand the grill not reading temperature accurately can get frustrating and troubleshooting can be time-consuming. Our grills read the temperature on an average, and the temperature variance is -/+25 F degrees. The most common contributor to any temperature management issue is low-quality or old pellets. Check the pellets at the end of the auger or in the firepot to make sure they have a nice sheen to them and have a nice "snap" to them when breaking. If the pellets crumble or look dull, try a fresh bag of pellets. If you change the temperature too often during a cook, this can cause issues with maintaining temperature. Instead, give time between changing temperatures so the grill can keep up with the changes. Properly working meat probes should read within ±7.5°F of the actual temperature. Traeger's wired meat probes provide readings that take an average over the entire length of the probe, which is why inserting the probe into the meat as much as possible will provide a more accurate reading. If your meat probe is still not reading temperature accurately, try calibrating the probe. Your grill does come with a 3-year warranty from the date of purchase. Please do not hesitate to reach out to us from 6 AM - 10 PM MT, 7 days a week, and one of our team members will get you squared away.

Temperature swings are a normal part of cooking on a Traeger as it's working to maintain a live fire in the pot at the bottom of the barrel. Our grills target an average temperature over the duration of the cook, much like your home oven does, so the results should still turn out as desired. Please note that use of the Super Smoke feature found on Timberline, Ironwood, and Silverton 820 models will cause the fluctuations to appear more drastic as it's adjusting the fire to produce heavier smoke.

Always be sure to strictly adhere to your grill's maintenance routine, and clean it after each particularly greasy cook. Allowing grease to build up can put your grill at risk of a grease fire, which can damage the grill's paint or worse. Paint damage from this will leave the barrel unprotected which will lead to rust.

Please don't hesitate to reach out with any questions or concerns, or check the wealth of information available on our Support page. We're always happy to help the Traegerhood.

ClientResponses.Response: Thank you for your review and feedback on our Timberline XL. We understand that searing can get frustrating if not cooked how you like it. Our favorite way to get a good sear is with our reverse sear method -- smoking your meat to about 15°F under your desired doneness level, removing it from heat while you crank up your grill's temperature, and then finishing to doneness on your hot Traeger. Did you know that an effective sear happens when the cooking surface is between 300°F and 500°F? While many people believe a grill needs to be over 500°F to get that caramelized crust on your meat, temperatures higher can result in dry food. Insert a cast iron grate or pan into your Traeger grill. Set your grill to 180 degrees. Smoke your meat until it is about 15°F below your desired doneness level, roughly an hour. Remove your meat from the grill. Turn your grill to HIGH, 450°F, or 500°F, depending on your model. Mix 2-3 pats of butter, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Once your grill heats up, place the meat back into your cast iron grate or pan. Sear your meat for about 3.5-4 minutes on each side, basting the meat with the butter mixture, until it reaches your desired internal temperature. Pull your steak off the grill and let it cool down for 10 minutes. Enjoy! If you have any questions or concerns please don’t hesitate to reach out to us from 6 am - 10 pm MT, 7 days a week, and one of our team members will get you squared away.

My second review since launch, this one being an update to the experience. A long review but absolutely needed.

Traeger delivers with smoking in regards to the pellet grill market. The problem is that is all it does with minimal smoke improvement from the regular Timberline series. As far as searing goes I have to say it's atrocious without the induction. Yes, that is why the induction is there but tbh, I don't always want to use a pan to sear on. The gimmick is "wood fired" by pellet grills and a lot of the time, I want to sear on the grill itself specifically on the thick grates they updated to. What you get in return however, is a baked piece of meat. This is due to the grills incapability to revert back to a high searing temp quickly when the lid opens for even a couple seconds to flip something. Again, I understand the idea of the induction but it shouldn't have to be mandatory to grill. Some may agree when I say this, sometimes you just want to grill. By grill I mean you want to reverse sear and do it on the grill with that specific heat source.

 If I could return it I would. If traeger did a buy back, I would! The problem is manufacturers know that people will be displeased in the grilling community if their products don't live up to the hype so their return policy is "un opened un used" so in the end you're left wanting more, wishing more, and a grill going hardly used. In the realm of pellet grills, this is good for smoking. For a deeper flavor there are better brands for that, specifically OJ and Webers smokefire but this is better usual in terms of build quality. 

After allll that text what is the final recommendation? I would say you need to seriously consider what you want in a pellet grill, how often you think you'll want to sear on a pan and not the actual grill, and whether the very basic function of this grill outside of it's bells and whistles are what you'll truly be happy with. This isn't something I would recommend to the average joe. This Traeger comes off as a status symbol in my opinion and for a guy like me who could care less about that, I am now stuck with something I really do not care for. 

At it's basic core, it can smoke. Is it good enough at that to spend this kind of money? No. Will you be stuck with it if you end up disliking it after a long term period? Probably. Going on a month and no one has nibbled on my listing for it. It's a hard pill to swallow when listing a grill so beyond low for what you spent and still, no one wants to take that dive. That speaks volumes.

Apparently this was a common thing and they shut down replacing lids until they corrected multiple damaged covers. It took 4 months to receive a new grill cover.

Second, I am now stuck in a "Downloading Updates" loop to where I can't even use the grill. I let it run for 2 1/2 hours. Called support, they told me to let it run overnight. I called support again today, they told me to let it run for the rest of the day. Something's broke here. It's not a signal strength issue - my access point is literally right next to it.  Support has been extremely rough, not knowing the product or even how to escalate when I can't even use the grill now for several days. One person said it will attempt to download 5 times, then not again, another person said 4 times - then they said it could take up to several weeks to update? What? I can't use my smoker for several weeks? Are you kidding me? This is a complete failure here. 

The vacuum system is no better than the 1300. They claim it goes into the bucket, but most of the ash is still in the main floor of the smoker where you have to suck it out anyways just like you did on the 1300. Cleaning is the same, features just the same, and I would say my 1300 maintained more consistent temperatures and less fluctuating temperatures. The XL does heat up much faster which is a plus. 

I'm really disappointed in this grill. Once I get this downloading updates issue fixed, I plan on putting it up on the market to sell so that I can go to a different smoker. I have been a Traeger fan for years and always viewed them as the gold standard for pellet smokers, this has really soured my opinion on the grills and their build quality and for my move off of them completely.

I have food on the grill!! Noooooo!!!!  Luckily I am a Mans Man and have now a total of 4 grills.  I left the XL on while I preheated my pro 780 and my Kamado.  I moved the food on to the other grills and after about an hour and a half with Traeger support and 2 full shutdown cycles, the code was cleared. I understand not being able to test the flame sensor while the grill in on, but the lid sensor code should be able to be tested and cleared while in use.  This was my first cook on it.  I am cooking again this weekend and if I don't have any issues, I may revise this to higher that 2 stars.  I cant express how disappointing this was to have this occur on the first cook on the most expensive grill that I have ever purchased. Had the support dropped the ball (which they did not), This review would have been titled "Returning my XL".  Thank you Traeger Support for your patients with me in this most trying of times. Results.ReviewText:
So this is my first Traeger and I went all in getting the XL. Beautiful grill, definitely for home us not competition. 
First I love the setting for the wired probes (has wireless more on that later) you can set the internal temps while maintaining a low smoke temp. It has a touch screen that is very user friendly with many features. The Timberline XL also has thick gauge stainless steel racks to last a long time. 
Now the problem: I had a party that I needed to cook a lot of food and the large cooking area was perfect. I wanted to use the wireless probes but could never get them to work nor had the time to call support. I had a whole top sirloin 2 pork butts and 1 whole packer and 1 flat to cook and all seemed to go well. Until I got to the stall. I wrapped the meats in foil and added the juice. At some point the juices worked their way out and down to the burner area. This coursed error code and this was late at night so no way to tear apart the grill and too hot as well as not knowing the grill. So the next day the sensor dried and fired up. After I was done and started the cleanup and discovered what I believe to be a flawed design. As you will see in the picture the base is designed to collect fluids on the left which worked well and collected fluid on the right which is the fire box. So you can’t cook any high fat meat nor use any fluid to break the stall on the right side dramatically killing 50% of your cooking surface. 
I do like the construction of the grill but my design would have a raised bevel to send juices to fat collector bucket not fire box. Traeger this needs to be fixed and parts sent out to customers. @ $3800 it’s the least you can do.

Results.ReviewText:
Traeger Technical Support Call Reference number: 01980833

TL:DR
Save your money for a grill that's not being Beta tested with paying customers. The kinks are NOT worked out with maintaining cook temperature.

I bought this grill over Memorial Day weekend 2022. I had high expectations for buying a premium smoker from a reputable company. The main function of the grill does not meet performance standards from my previous Ironwood 650 Traeger smoker. Per the representative, the acceptable tolerance for temperature variation is 25°F +/-.  This is trouble when trying to smoke ribs with the 3/2/1 recipe. I set the grill at 180° and would maintain temps ranging from 150°F- 165°F. This prolonged my cook from 6 hours to 9 hours based on meat temperature.. I'm order to keep the temperature at goal I would intermittently jack the temperature to above 180°F and dial down once goal was met. When calling customer service they were happy to tell me my average cook temperature was 175°F (thanks WiFire).  I stopped doing my workaround and the tech support was able to see the discrepancy in temperature.

Their recommendation was to run the grill's seasoning cycle... Again. I was frustrated to learn that there is an entire Beta team that was talked to fixed the issues with this grill.  These issues were known and Traeger still moved this grill to market.

Because of these cook issues the $100 worth of ribs (6 racks) were tough because of the extended cook times. I had to ensure the pork was safe to eat and not undercooked. The variants in cook temp caused doubt.

I asked to be compensated for the waste in Pellets and meat related to a sub- performing product. I called in 5/29 and was told that a manager will review the call and reach out to me. Review will stand until this situation is remedied. If no contact, then I'll be returning the grill to purchase a better performing grill.

Bluetooth temperature probe would disconnect from Bluetooth mid cook. Unable to set/reset temperature goals mid cook.

Results.ReviewText: When I saw the videos, I knew I had to have one.  I have an Ironwood 885 and wanted something larger. Went to my local Ace Hardware and purchased Timberline XL. They assembled it and delivered it. Followed the instructions to the letter, loaded up the pellets and started the seasoning cycle. The Smoker would not get past 190 degrees and went into the shutdown cycle. Tried again, same results. Contacted Trager support by text and that did not work well at all. Suddenly I see a message on the grill screen. It said, temperature sensor error and also said for me to take the drip pan out, the heat shield, and vacuum out the dust, pellets in the hot pot and try again. I'm thinking what dust?  It never heated up. I'm thinking I have an electrical issue with the sensor. Not happy at this point. After I calmed down, I decided to do what they asked before I called Ace to come get this thing.  As soon as I took it apart the problem was very obvious. There is a stainless steel sleave that fits inside the chute the pellets drop through to get to the hot pot. The sleave was not installed correctly, and the lip on the top was partially blocking the pellets coming from the auger and they were bypassing the chute. Only a few were actually getting into hot pot and igniting. I removed the sleeve, reinstalled it correctly. Put everything back together and tried again. Worked perfectly. Heated right up.  After the seasoning cycle was over, I put on two Tri-Tips and enjoyed a perfect cook. Used the two MEATER Probes that came with the Smoker, and all was fantastic.  Good luck Traeger trying to top this one. You just lost a customer as I don't think I will be in the market for another Smoker for many years to come.

Results.ReviewText:
I’d love to give them a 5 – and certainly do for the food, but for the product, I have to drop to a 3. So I’ll make it a generous overall 4. I think they rolled it out before it was ready. Customers should never be the Quality Assurance department, and at this price point, there should be zero issues.
I have been using a lump charcoal smoker (Komodo style) for years, so know my way around smoking food. I was looking for a Natural Gas Grill for an outdoor kitchen I am building. I found the new Traeger Timberline and it said it was both a smoker and a grill, so I figured, one grill doing both products: Great! My lump charcoal smoker can also be used as a grill, but I liked the idea of "set it and forget it" temperature.
Well, yes you can grill on it, but the first time it took 1 hour and 45 minutes to get to 450-degree. I was on the phone with support for an hour of that - maybe more. I ended up eating a ham sandwich for dinner.
The second time it was quicker – 45 minutes. On a call with support, they told me the grill "learns" and will get faster each time. I hope so, because if it continues like this may end up with a gas grill anyway. They also said it takes loner because the heat is “indirect heat”. It is not like a gas or charcoal grill where the meat is right above the flames. Makes sense.
I will say this - the steaks were terrific.
I cooked a couple whole chickens at 350-degrees. I smoked them first at 225 for an hour, the brought it up to 350. Didn’t notice any issues with the temp. It got to 225 within 15 minutes and I wasn’t watching it go to 350 – I was watching the meat temperature. They were terrific too – very moist.
Smoked a 10-lb pork butt – very happy with that cook. Smoked for 22 hours with real issues.
I have no complaints about the food cooked in this – just the time to temp when grilling – and I hope that improves. It seems like it is.
Issues:
My second wireless probe never syncs to the grill.
The hopper is a poor design. It does hold an entire bag, but the hopper creates a hollow tunnel – like a whirlpool – where the pellets drop into the fire chamber. The pellet sensor is right over that, so I keep getting alerts that I am low on pellets, and I must move the pellets around in the hopper to make it happy again. Not cool on long cooks.
The grill seems to send a “Pre-Heat Finished” alert after 15 minutes – never when the grill is actually to the goal temperature. I’ve mentioned this to Traeger support while on my calls with them – they say they are looking into this.
Don’t buy this expecting to get rid of your gas grill. This isn’t that.
Doesn’t hold temp as well as expected. The walls are single wall construction, so it makes sense – I just wasn’t expecting it to vary as much as it did – about 10-degrees hotter at times, and a few degrees cooler. 
On the plus side:
The wireless technology is very good. My old lump charcoal smoker had a third party device that controlled the temperature and such, but it worked off Bluetooth. That was horrible. This thing lets me know what’s going on no matter where I am in the house. That’s a huge point in favor of this.
Does a great smoke flavor. I don’t notice the smoke rings that I saw on the lump charcoal, but definitely taste it.
The end result is a really tasty meal.
Traeger has exceptional customer support. I have never called for support and had the level of service these guys provide. They certainly set the bar for customer support.
Results.Title: It's a Smoker

Results.ReviewText:
I was a little reluctant to buy the grill having read the reviews. Been waiting a few years to buy a Timberline in hope they’d add the ability to have a front shelf.
I went ahead and purchased thinking, most people will take the time to post a review over a negative experience than a positive.
So, we unboxed it. Followed the instructions to a “T”. I’m not going to lie, I was a littler nervous when the seasoning routing didn’t get to the temp is had set. Afterward, the firmware updated.
We decided to review the grill…had also seen reviews it wouldn’t get to temp.
Set 500 and restarted it. Saw reviews about slow to get to temp, but it hit 500 in about 14 minutes. Not bad really.
We normally cook 225, so we lowered it. It kept a nice range.
Tried Super Smoke. Worked good too.
Probes paired without issue.
The app was a little flakey initially, saying the grill wasn’t online, when I knew it was because I could see it connected when I connected to my router.

So, maybe we’re lucky, I don’t know, but we absolutely love this grill.
Cooked ribeye, tritip, and salmon so far. Everything has come off tasting fantastic. We’re doing ribs right now and have a brisket set for the weekend.
The “only” negative is the pellet bin that comes with it. Somebody in quality control needs a talking to because it fails the Traeger name miserably. The bin cannot handle a full bag of pellets. It bows outward and loses its seal. That’s just basic there. Why would someone not test a bag of Traeger pellets in the bin? Like I said, complete quality control failure there. I hope Traeger does something quickly because the bins are like $30 and they’re complete crap. Pardon my French. We use ours to empty the hopper, then pour the pellets into a better container.

The grill though…we love it. Zero complaints.

Results.ReviewText: Long but worth the read.  I was never a fan of Traeger, because I’ve always felt their grills didn’t get hot enough and didn’t smoke enough.  Well, after 4 weeks of vacillating, I took the plunge.  However, I refused to by this from anyone (including Traeger) that had a no return policy.   So I waited until Home Depot got it.  Well this new  xl gets crazy hot and smokes like a chimney.  The induction works great, and let’s just be honest, this grill on your deck makes you the talk of the town, because it looks incredible.  But at the end of the day, it all comes down to if the thing works.   First week, whole chicken, ribs, and chicken breast were absolutely amazing.  The smoke flavor was what you would expect and them some.  Then came week two.  Halfway through an 8 hour pork butt, I get a flame sensor error.  I call Traeger and they say I can finish the cook, but the grill won’t perform optimally.  Well, it stopped performing completely, and I had to fire up my trusty old Pitboss.  After trouble shooting and shining a light down into the fire pot toward the auger, the error code was gone.  They said it shouldn’t happen again.  Well, the next day, temperatures all 30% higher or lower than what I set it to, and then, the following day, another flame sensor error, right after I’ve prepped my wings to cook.  So those go back in the fridge and I spend time 30 more minutes on the phone with Traeger, with the solution being to simply fix it the way we did last time.  At that point, I was done,  so back to the store it went.  At the end of the day, this grill looks great, has great features, ideas, and concepts, but when I spend my own hard-earned money at the tune of 4K and more for the accessories, I need this grill to be flawless out the box, and not give me any issue for at least a couple years.  These were major issues, twice in the middle of a cook, and once right before a cook.   This grill should have been a home run,  but it just seems like there’s just too many moving parts adding up to too many potential problems.  And the fact that it was released with these and other issues I’m reading about is very disappointing.  All of this from a person who never writes reviews unless I’m completely blown away, or utterly disappointed.  In this case, it is definitely the latter.
